bullets.title: Iran-US ceasefire drives broad risk-on; tech/semis lead, oil drops to ~$78-79
bullets.body: A 60-day Iran-US ceasefire MOU (signing ceremony expected June 19) triggered a sharp risk-on impulse: S&P +1.7% to within 90bps of ATH, Nasdaq/NDX +3.1%, Semis +5.45%, Mag7 +2.7%, while WTI fell ~3% to ~$78.35. Core disputes on nuclear program, missiles, and proxies remain unresolved, and JPM flags Hormuz-reopening trades (airlines, housing) are vulnerable to fade after the initial impulse. Wall Street banks (Citi, MS, GS) cut Q3/Q4 Brent forecasts; GS moved 2026 Q4 Brent to $80 from $90.

bullets.title: Memory complex explodes higher; HDD cycle elongation thesis gaining conviction
bullets.body: WDC +16%, MU +10.8%, STX +9.43%, SNDK +6.45% on Monday with further pre-market strength (WDC +8.5%, STX +6.3%). Morgan Stanley raised STX PT to $1,035 and WDC to $650 based on Asia checks showing HDD demand growing 40-50% annually vs. supply growth of 30-35%, with shortages expected through at least CY28; current nearline HDD price/TB under $15 with vendors targeting $25-30 over 2-3 years. STX and WDC FY28 EPS estimates now ~70% above Street consensus.

bullets.title: Fed expected hawkish Wednesday; dot plot may show no cuts until 2028, up to 6 hike dots
bullets.body: FOMC meeting Wednesday marks new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's inaugural policy statement. UBS expects removal of easing bias with as many as 6 dots voting for hikes this year, and the dot plot likely showing no cuts until 2028. US 10y expected to trade at 4.50% this quarter before falling to 4.25% by year-end; 10y currently +2bps to 4.44% pre-market. Economists broadly anticipate rate hikes may be necessary by end-2026 despite Iran deal.

bullets.title: AI capex supercycle accelerating; $5.5T estimated through 2030, MSFT flagged as 1 year behind
bullets.body: JPM raised AI capex estimates to $5.5T through 2030 with 138 GW data center capacity growth as base case; GOOG and AMZN each aggressively pre-funding $300-350B FY27-28 ramps while MSFT is flagged as 1 year behind with a $90-130B funding gap. AVGO/Apollo/Blackstone structured a $30B AI XPV JV at ~6% cost of capital as a potential public-market financing paradigm. Agentic workloads consuming 23x more tokens than conversational tasks, creating token cost constraints on enterprise adoption.

bullets.title: BoJ hikes 25bps to 1.0% (31-year high); ECB seen adding one more hike in September
bullets.body: Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.0% in a 7-1 vote, keeping bond tapering unchanged; market reaction was modest. ECB is expected to deliver one more hike in September with modest risk of a third. Falling oil prices reduce near-term pressure on BoE, BoJ, and ECB. BoJ may consider suspension of bond purchase reductions, potentially causing curve flattening.

bullets.title: UBS raises AC World target to 1200 YE, cuts recession risk to 5%, raises bubble probability to 50%
bullets.body: UBS equity strategy raised the MSCI AC World target to 1200 by year-end (from 1120, current 1131), cutting recession risk to 5% while raising bubble probability to 50%. The firm recommends staying long but rotating into de-rated cyclicals. Goldman similarly characterizes the macro as a 'Post-Modern Cycle' with a structural capex supercycle (AI, defense, infrastructure) shifting returns to earnings growth vs. multiple expansion, favoring capital-intensive sectors.

bullets.title: Semiconductor momentum overbought near-term; SOXL saw ~$9B buy at close, leveraged ETF risk flagged
bullets.body: The High Beta Momentum Factor Exposure is up 54.9% YTD after rising 3.2% on Monday. SOXL (3x Semis Bull) had ~$9B buy orders at close to maintain flows while SOXS crashed -16% on 456M shares as retail hedges unwound. JPM notes leveraged ETF usage in semis could present pullback risk; SPX immediate-term risk range is 7,266-7,645, with the gamma flip at 7,403. QQQ 1M implied vol declined to 22.6 (86th percentile) but remains below realized vol of 23.9.

bullets.title: NVDA raising $20-25B investment-grade bonds; described as benchmark creation, not capex funding
bullets.body: NVIDIA is set to raise at least $20-25B through investment-grade corporate bonds for general corporate purposes and debt refinancing. Analysts characterize the issuance as creating a liquid benchmark rather than signaling capex need, given NVDA generated $49B free cash flow in its latest quarter with FY2026 revenue of $216B (vs. $27B when it last raised debt in 2021). NVDA stock was +3.5% Monday despite the deal.

bullets.title: CPO tech delayed to 2030-31; WFE forecasts $200B+ in CY27, $250B+ in CY28 on AI demand
bullets.body: Co-packaged optics (CPO) scale-up is delayed to 2030-31 due to interposer overheating, which will pressure demand for CW laser, OE, FAU, and optical fiber. Separately, wafer fab equipment forecasts point to $200B+ in CY27 and $250B+ potential in CY28 driven by relentless AI infrastructure demand. AMAT is flagged as a top pick with accelerating Semi Systems growth and strong positioning in DRAM, Logic, and Advanced Packaging.

bullets.title: China May retail sales turn negative YoY for first time since COVID; online resilient at +3.4%
bullets.body: China total retail sales fell 0.6% YoY in May 2026, the first sub-zero monthly print since Q4 2022 and below the -0.2% consensus. Online retail sales grew 3.4% YoY (up from 2.3% in April), providing partial offset. Discretionary categories remain severely weak: electronics/appliances -15.6%, gold/jewelry -8.9%. China Q2 GDP is tracking softer at 4.4% despite export strength, and fixed asset investment came in at +4.1% vs. consensus +4.3%.

bullets.title: Fox acquiring Roku for $22B ($160/sh, 60% cash/40% stock); 7 analysts downgrade ROKU
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku for $160/share ($22B EV), with FOXA shareholders owning ~73% post-close. The deal is dilutive to FCF/sh ~12% in FY28 but accretive +3% FY29; pro-forma net leverage 2.8x at close, de-levering to ~1x by FY29. Seven analysts downgraded ROKU (JPM, Piper Sandler, Susquehanna, Evercore, Wolfe, Citizens, Loop) with price targets clustering at $155-160, reflecting the deal value and low probability of a competing bid. FOXA fell ~17% on dilution concerns.

bullets.title: Qualcomm in $8-10B Tenstorrent acquisition talks to build out AI chip capabilities
bullets.body: Qualcomm is in discussions to acquire RISC-V AI acceleration startup Tenstorrent for $8-10B; Intel was also reportedly in prior talks. CEO Jim Keller brings Zen/Tesla semiconductor expertise; Tenstorrent is strong in inferencing and edge technology. QCOM trades at ~20x forward vs. ARM at ~175x, with persistent skepticism on Apple revenue loss ($5B/11%) offset by automotive/IoT diversification.

bullets.title: IT Services/ACN weak as AI crowds out traditional spend; MS downgrades ACN to EW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley downgraded Accenture to Equal Weight from Overweight, cutting PT to $177 from $240, citing AI spend crowding out traditional IT services. CY26 IT Services budget growth is only ~2% YoY as AI pilots have yet to demonstrate clear returns. UBS takes the opposite view, upgrading ACN citing its ~11x forward valuation and AI additive via integration demand rather than displacement; ACN earnings Thursday with consensus at $3.71 EPS/$18.78B revenue.

bullets.title: DeepSeek raises $7.4B+ at $50B+ valuation; ByteDance accessing 36,000 NVDA B200s via Malaysia
bullets.body: DeepSeek is raising over CNY50B ($7.4B+) in its first external funding round at a valuation exceeding $50B, with Tencent (CNY10B), CATL (CNY5B), JD.com, and China's national AI fund in final talks; shares carry a 5-year lockup. Separately, ByteDance is reportedly accessing ~36,000 NVIDIA B200 chips via Malaysia-based Aolani Cloud at an estimated cost above $2.5B, with unconfirmed reports of 150,000 GB300 GPU pursuit. The US-China AI capability gap is widening from 8% to 13% on export controls.

bullets.title: MLCC lead times extending to 24 weeks; AI servers require 2x the component count of conventional
bullets.body: Global MLCC lead times have extended from ~10 weeks to 24 weeks with 20-40% price increases. A single AI server requires ~28,000 MLCCs vs. 13,000 for conventional servers; NVDA Rubin uses 12,000 MLCCs per board vs. 6,500 in GB200. Murata expects peak MLCC demand around 2028 potentially extending to 2030, and is planning ¥250B FY2026 capex. TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is expected to narrow from 20% to 10% by end-2026 as monthly capacity reaches 120-140k wafers/month.

bullets.title: Global AI capex financing: Broadcom backs $35B Anthropic chip order; $8-9T US MMF wall of money
bullets.body: Broadcom is backing a $35B Anthropic AI chip order to finance 20+ GW of compute capacity. Jefferies notes $8-9T in US money market funds provides ongoing liquidity support for markets. Global time on GenAI apps is projected to double YoY in H1 2026 (17.2B to 36B hours). AI-referred retail traffic spends 53% more per visit and browses longer than non-AI traffic per Adobe Analytics May data.

bullets.title: CRM acquires Fin for $3.6B to expand Agentforce; Fin's Apex model outperforms GPT-5.4
bullets.body: Salesforce is acquiring Fin (formerly Intercom) for ~$3.6B all-cash (~9x trailing ARR), expected to close F4Q27 with no guidance change. Fin's AI Agent product is at $100M+ ARR growing ~350% YoY; its proprietary Apex model outperforms GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.5 on customer service benchmarks with 65% fewer hallucinations. The deal targets SMB/mid-market as a land-and-expand wedge; UBS maintains Neutral at $185 PT questioning the strategic need after 2 years of Agentforce R&D.

bullets.title: MSFT turns to AWS for GitHub capacity surge; GitHub commits on pace for 14B in 2026 vs 1B in 2025
bullets.body: Microsoft is turning to Amazon AWS to handle GitHub AI-driven capacity surge despite a plan to migrate fully to Azure by 2027. GitHub commits are on pace for 14 billion in 2026 vs. 1 billion in 2025, a 14x YoY surge driven by AI coding tools. The episode highlights the unevenness of hyperscaler AI infrastructure buildouts and MSFT's flagged $90-130B FY27-28 capex funding gap.

bullets.title: Biopharma lagging YTD (DRG +4%, XBI +12% vs SPX +10.6%) but Citi bullish on H2 catalysts
bullets.body: The biopharma sector has underperformed YTD despite +13% projected earnings growth in 2026 and a ~17x forward P/E, which Citi views as undervaluation. A packed H2 2026 catalyst calendar, healthy M&A/BD cadence, and defensive attributes are cited as reasons to expect catch-up. Iran conflict headlines and AI-led tech trade dominance since early March have weighed on sector sentiment.

bullets.title: Taiwan AI power demand CAGR doubling to 2.3% through 2035; US LNG now 40%+ of Taiwan imports
bullets.body: UBS estimates AI-driven growth will double Taiwan's power demand CAGR from ~1.1% (2015-25) to ~2.3% (2026-35), with 4M26 growth already at 2.5% ahead of government forecasts. Taiwan will need ~4.4 mtpa additional LNG by 2030 and 9.3 mtpa by 2035 (19-40% of 2025 imports). US LNG supplied over 40% of Taiwan imports in April (up from 7% in March), replacing disrupted Gulf flows. Grid infrastructure and power equipment are identified as key bottlenecks.
